name: Jebel Jais
distance: About 1h45–2h from Dubai; about 30–45 minutes from Ras Al Khaimah city
desc: The UAE's highest mountain massif in the Hajar range: a paved road to a viewing deck at 1,250m, the Jais Flight zipline, mountain camps and air usually about 10°C cooler than the coast.
area: Hajar Mountains, above Ras Al Khaimah city, on the border with Oman's Musandam
bestTime: October to April, arriving early; Jais Flight and the other activities have fixed hours, and the road is best driven in daylight and clear weather.
timeNeeded: 2–3 hours for the drive and the viewing deck; half a day or more with a zipline booking, a meal or a hike.
fees: Driving up is free with no entry permit (as announced in February 2026); Jais Viewing Deck Park charges AED 10 a person including VAT; the zipline, restaurant and camps are paid, bookable extras.
hours: The operator says the mountain is open 24/7, but it closes for seasonal maintenance and after storms (see the note above). When open, Viewing Deck Park runs Sunday–Thursday 8am–8pm and Friday–Saturday 8am–11pm; activities and restaurants keep fixed, seasonal hours.

access.note: The road up is fully paved and any normal car can drive it; the operator says to drive carefully in fog or rain. There is no fuel on the mountain road, so fill up before you climb.

facilities.note: Jais Viewing Deck Park has two cafés (Puro Express and Muse Café), seven viewing decks and solar lighting; 1484 by Puro is a restaurant that needs a reservation. Toilets at the deck park are reported as limited by one third-party guide, and no source confirmed mobile signal.

gpsSource: https://www.maploco.com/top-attractions/jebel-jais/viewing-deck-park/ lists Jais Viewing Deck Park at 25.93738, 56.13098, roughly 1,250m up the mountain road; this is consistent with Wikimedia Commons photos geotagged around the upper road and with OpenStreetMap's Jais Flight and 1484 by Puro nodes about 1.5km north-east. It is the visitor area, not the summit (which is on the Omani side).
body:
Jebel Jais is the high massif of the northern Hajar Mountains in Ras Al Khaimah, and it is usually called the UAE's highest mountain. Tourism sites give its height as 1,934 metres, but that summit sits just across the border in Oman's Musandam; the highest point on the UAE side is about 1,892 metres, and the highest peak lying wholly inside the UAE is nearby Jabal Ar Rahrah, at around 1,691 metres. In short, Jebel Jais is the UAE's highest mountain mass, with its summit on the border.

You can drive most of the way up. A paved, signposted road of roughly 30km climbs from the edge of Ras Al Khaimah city, with many hairpin bends. It suits an ordinary car, and there is no fuel on the way. Most visitors pull in at Jais Viewing Deck Park, 1,250 metres above sea level, with seven viewing decks, binoculars and two cafés, looking across the Hajar range and, on clear days, towards the Gulf.

The mountain has become an adventure destination. Jais Flight, which opened in 2018 and is billed as the world's longest zipline, runs 2.83km at up to 150km/h and takes around three minutes. Beside it sit the Jais Sky Tour zipline circuit, a sledder, a via ferrata, 1484 by Puro restaurant, Camp 1770 and the Bear Grylls Explorers Camp, plus marked hiking trails. Almost all of these are separate, bookable experiences; the drive itself is free, and Viewing Deck Park charges AED 10.

The climate is why people come. Visit Ras Al Khaimah says the mountain is usually about 10°C cooler than other parts of the emirate, and Wikipedia's 2003–2021 climate record shows a mean annual temperature of 19.0°C, a record June high of 36.5°C and a record February low of -5.7°C. Snow is rare, but it has been documented. The practical catch is that operations are seasonal and weather-dependent: storms closed the mountain in December 2025, and the season is October to April. Check current status before you set out.

guide.gettingThere: From Dubai, take the E311 or E611 towards Ras Al Khaimah; the official operator's guide puts the drive at between 1h45 and 2h. The mountain road begins outside Ras Al Khaimah city, about 30 to 45 minutes from central hotels, and is a single paved, signposted route with parking areas at intervals. A normal car is all you need. There are no fuel stations on the mountain road, so fill up before the ascent. Without a car, the operator lists taxis as an option, and RAK buses link Dubai with Ras Al Khaimah city; a bus service up the mountain itself was not confirmed for the current season. If you plan to go beyond the viewing deck for the zipline, restaurant or camps, book first: entry to those is by reservation.
guide.whenToGo: October to April is the season for activities, hiking and camping, and it is when the mountain's own operations run. The operator says the mountain is open 24/7, but activities keep fixed hours: Jais Flight's published winter slots run roughly 9:30am to 4pm and it is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, with summer slots later in the day, and the Sky Tour and via ferrata run Wednesday to Sunday. Arrive early in the cooler months, when visitor numbers peak. Storms can close the mountain at short notice (it was shut after the heavy rain of December 2025 and reopened on 31 January 2026), and one third-party tracker reported a seasonal closure from mid-September 2026 with no reopening date, so confirm the current status with the operator before you drive up.
guide.onSite: Jais Viewing Deck Park is the usual first stop: seven viewing decks, binoculars, Puro Express and Muse Café, and a view of the zipline in action. Jais Flight is 2.83km long, reaches up to 150km/h and takes about three minutes; riders must weigh between 40kg and 120kg, wear closed-toe shoes with grip and athletic clothing (no dresses or skirts), and carry original photo ID. The minimum height is published as 122cm by the operator's FAQ and 130cm on Visit Ras Al Khaimah's page, so confirm when booking. Under-18s need a parent or guardian and a signed waiver. Visit Ras Al Khaimah lists tickets from AED 325, varying by season; check the booking page for the current price. 1484 by Puro needs a confirmed reservation. Marked hiking trails run from easy walks to harder mountain routes; trail work was under way at Wadi Khammed and Hidden Oasis in September 2026.
guide.safety: The road is paved but steep and winding, with many hairpins, and the operator advises driving carefully in fog or rain; use the pull-ins rather than stopping on the carriageway. Weather is the main risk. Heavy rain in December 2025 (127mm over two days, according to The National) forced a full closure, and a major rockslide on a steep section of road was reported when the mountain reopened in January 2026, so expect closures and entry limits after storms. Camping in wadis is strongly discouraged because of flash flooding. The mountain is usually about 10°C cooler than the rest of the emirate, but winter nights can be properly cold: carry a jacket, as temperatures can drop sharply and have gone below freezing. In summer it is still hot, with a June record high of 36.5°C. For hikes, carry plenty of water, wear proper footwear, tell someone your route and stay on marked trails.
guide.heritage: People have been connected to this mountain for thousands of years: the operator notes ancient rock carvings and remnants of old settlements, and describes more than 70 million years of geological change. Native plants include wild fig and sidr trees, and wildlife includes mountain foxes and goats. A biodiversity survey reported by The National in September 2026 identified 45 plant species, 29 bird species and eight mammals, including the Arabian red fox, Afro-Asiatic wildcat and Brandt's hedgehog. Snow is documented but rare: Wikipedia lists snowfall in January 2009 (described as only the second time on record in the UAE) and a mix of snow and hail in January 2020, while the UAE's lowest recorded temperature, -5.7°C, was reported on the mountain's slopes on 3 February 2017.
guide.etiquette: Take all rubbish with you: fines for littering and for lighting fires start at around AED 500, according to reports, and cutting trees or collecting firewood is prohibited. Keep noise down at viewpoints and leave the rock art and vegetation untouched.

glance.how: Paved road, any car; no fuel on the mountain
glance.time: 2–3 hours; half a day with a zipline
glance.cost: Road free; Viewing Deck Park AED 10; activities extra

faqs.a: Official tourism sites give 1,934 metres. Wikipedia says that summit is on the Omani side of the border and puts the highest point inside the UAE at 1,892 metres, so the figure you will see depends on the source.

faqs.q: Is Jebel Jais the highest mountain in the UAE?
faqs.a: It is widely billed as the UAE's highest peak. Wikipedia adds that its summit lies in Oman, and that Jabal Ar Rahrah (1,691 metres) is the highest peak entirely within the UAE. Calling it the UAE's highest mountain mass is the safest wording.

faqs.q: Can you drive up Jebel Jais, and is there a fee?
faqs.a: Yes. The road is fully paved and open to ordinary cars, and in February 2026 Khaleej Times reported that entry permits were no longer needed. Jais Viewing Deck Park charges AED 10 a person; the zipline, restaurant and camps are booked and paid for separately.

faqs.q: Can you camp on Jebel Jais?
faqs.a: Camp 1770 (at 1,770 metres) and the Bear Grylls Explorers Camp are the bookable options. Guides report informal camping at roadside viewpoints, but we found no official statement of permitted areas. Avoid wadis because of flash floods, and note that reported fines for littering and fires start around AED 500.

faqs.q: How much colder is Jebel Jais than the coast, and does it snow?
faqs.a: Visit Ras Al Khaimah says it is usually about 10°C cooler than other parts of the emirate. Snow is rare but documented, in January 2009 and January 2020, and the UAE's lowest temperature on record, -5.7°C, was reported on the mountain on 3 February 2017.

faqs.q: What are the Jais Flight zipline's length, limits and price?
faqs.a: It is 2.83km long, reaches up to 150km/h and takes about three minutes. Riders must weigh 40 to 120kg; the minimum height is 122cm (operator FAQ) or 130cm (Visit Ras Al Khaimah), and under-18s need a guardian's signed waiver. Tickets are listed from AED 325, varying by season.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Jebel Jais?
faqs.a: October to April, when the season runs and temperatures are comfortable. Arrive early in the cooler months, when visitor numbers peak.

faqs.q: Is Jebel Jais open right now?
faqs.a: Not always. It closes for seasonal maintenance and after heavy rain; a September 2026 report said it was shut for maintenance with no reopening date yet. Check visitjebeljais.com or call ahead on the day.

seoTitle: Jebel Jais, RAK: Drive, Zipline, Camping & Weather
seoDesc: Jebel Jais in Ras Al Khaimah: its height explained, the paved road up, Jais Flight zipline limits, camping, weather, snow and the best time to go.

productLink.sentence: Jebel Jais belongs to the Hajar range, and the peaks traced on {{link}} are those above Wadi Naqab, also in Ras Al Khaimah, a nearby stretch of the same mountains rather than Jebel Jais itself.

_doubts: SUMMIT HEIGHT: official/tourism sources (Visit RAK, visitjebeljais.com, MoET) say 1,934 m; Wikipedia says that summit is in Oman (Musandam) and gives 1,892 m as the UAE-side high point; the Wikipedia Jabal Ar Rahrah page lists Jebel Jais at 1,911 m and calls Rahrah (1,691 m) the highest mountain entirely in the UAE. The text reports all of these rather than choosing one. No official survey was found to settle it.

CURRENT STATUS CONFLICT: visitjebeljais.com FAQs say the mountain is 'open 24/7' year-round, and Visit RAK lists summer zipline slots, but WOW-RAK (a third-party site, updated 14 Sep 2026) says the whole mountain, including the road, deck park and hiking, is closed for the summer/maintenance with no reopening date. The National (15 Sep 2026) does not mention a closure. Not independently confirmed from an official source; the page hedges and tells readers to check. Re-check before publishing, since 1 Oct is near the start of the 2026/27 season.

ENTRY RULES: Khaleej Times (3 Feb 2026) reported a temporary rule requiring a booking or an AED 10 Viewing Deck ticket to go up; Khaleej Times (11 Feb 2026) and CairoScene (10 Mar 2026) then said all restrictions were lifted and no entry permit is needed. The AED 10 deck park ticket is still listed on visitjebeljais.com (AED 10 incl. 5% VAT, valid one day); it is unclear whether the deck park charge is enforced for every visitor now. WOW-RAK says AED 5, which looks outdated.

ZIPLINE PRICE: Visit RAK says 'starting at AED 325 (varies by season)'; visitjebeljais.com mentions AED 360–450 in Oct–Mar for 'specialised experiences' without naming which; third-party sellers vary. Only the AED 325 'from' figure is used and hedged. Prices may be out of date.

ZIPLINE LIMITS: weight 40–120 kg is consistent on Visit RAK and the operator FAQ (the deck park page oddly says 40–100 kg for its listing). Minimum height is 130 cm on Visit RAK and 122 cm on the operator FAQ; both are reported. No minimum age was stated; Visit RAK only says under-18s need a guardian and a signed waiver.

ZIPLINE LENGTH/RECORD: Visit RAK and operators say 2.83 km and 'world's longest'; Wikipedia gives 2,832 m, opened February 2018, up to 150 km/h (Visit RAK elsewhere says speeds of 120–150 km/h). Only the 'billed as' wording is used; the Guinness record itself was not verified at the source.

ZIPLINE HOURS: Visit RAK says winter 9:30am–4pm, summer 10:30am and 5pm slots, closed Mon/Tue; WOW-RAK says activities run Wed–Sun from 9:30am; Khaleej Times says Sky Tour runs Wed–Sun and public holidays. Hours may have changed.

ROAD LENGTH: Wikipedia says 36 km (completed 2019); the operator's staycation page says 28 km of paved road for cyclists from foot to summit area. Text says 'roughly 30 km'. The number of hairpin bends was not found in any source and is not stated. Wikipedia's remark that the upper road is closed to the public dates from December 2019 and may be outdated.

DRIVE TIMES: visitjebeljais.com blog says 1h45–2h from Dubai and 30–40 min from RAK city to the mountain base; the FAQ says about 2h and about 45 min; WOW-RAK says 90 min–2h and about 50 min. Ranges used.

GPS: 25.9374, 56.131 is Maploco's coordinate for Jais Viewing Deck Park. Kidzapp lists 25.953056, 56.183889 for the 'viewing deck park', but that matches the OpenStreetMap summit node (25.9534, 56.1843) on the Omani side, so it was not used. OpenStreetMap places Jais Flight and 1484 by Puro at about 25.9472, 56.1400. No official coordinate was found; confirm on the ground. 1484 by Puro is said to be at 1,484 m, the deck park at 1,250 m, and one source says the restaurant is 'at the site', so the exact layout of the upper area is unclear.

CAMPING: no official RAK or Marjan statement of where camping is permitted was found (Time Out's camping guide could not be fetched). PropertyFinder (Feb 2026) and Arabian Wanderers say informal roadside camping near the numbered viewpoints is tolerated and mention three government-designated public campsites; this is not confirmed by an official source, so the text only says it is 'reported'. Camp 1770 (1,770 m) and Bear Grylls Explorers Camp are bookable per Visit RAK; no prices were found. Littering/fire fines of about AED 500 come from PropertyFinder and a 2022 Zawya article and may have changed.

FACILITIES: toilets at the deck park are described as 'limited' only by WOW-RAK (third party); no source confirmed parking charges, prayer room or mobile signal, so signal is 'unknown'. Visitjebeljais.com lists Puro Express and Muse Café at the deck park and 1484 by Puro and Red Rock BBQ elsewhere on the mountain; opening days and times of these differ between pages (1484 by Puro: 8am–8pm daily per Gulf Business in January 2026; Mon–Fri 8am–6pm, closed Tue per the operator's staycation blog) and are not given in the text.

WEATHER: the 'about 10°C cooler' figure is Visit RAK's wording ('usually'). Wikipedia's climate figures (mean 19.0°C, record high 36.5°C June, record low -5.7°C February, 2003–2021) are used as given. The -5.7°C on 3 Feb 2017 UAE-record claim comes from Gulf News, which does not cite NCM; no NCM page was opened. Snow: only January 2009 and January 2020 (Wikipedia) are cited; Wikipedia also lists February 2017 but describes only the temperature, so snow is not claimed for that date.

FLOOD/ROCKSLIDE: The National (23 Dec 2025) reported 127 mm of rain over two days and a full closure; Khaleej Times (3 Feb 2026) reported the January 2026 reopening followed 'severe weather and a major rockslide'. Dates are as reported by those outlets.
ARABIC NAME: 'جبل جيس' comes from the OpenStreetMap peak node name and the brief; no tourism source opened gave the Arabic.

NOT FOUND: no source gave a fog frequency, mobile signal coverage, or a documented UAE-side road closure for fog; 'drive carefully during fog or rain' is the operator's FAQ wording only. The public bus to the mountain (weekends to end of April, per a Platinumlist guide) was not confirmed for 2026/27 and is not in the text.

1 Oct 2026 review: removed unsourced figures (zipline launch altitude, Sky Tour line count, trail count and total length, the claim that the public road stops short of the top). Re-verify current opening status, deck-park fee and zipline price on the day before publishing.

notice: WOW-RAK, a local guide site, reported on 14 September 2026 that the mountain road, Viewing Deck Park and Jais Flight were closed for seasonal maintenance, with no reopening date announced. The operator's own site still says the mountain is open. It usually reopens as the weather cools, so check visitjebeljais.com or call ahead on the day before you drive up.
